w:r.w:t: The Terminal Tracking Application is a purpose-built, standalone web application designed for Terminal Distributor — a global payment terminal distributor managing thousands of serialised payment devices across a worldwide warehouse network. The application serves as the master system of record for terminal serial number states, inventory counts, order management, and cost tracking.

The core problem is visibility: Terminal Distributor currently lacks a unified system to answer fundamental operational questions — where is a specific terminal right now, what state is it in, is it available, when will it arrive, and how much has it cost? This PRD defines the requirements to build a lean, web-based solution that resolves these gaps.
The application is designed in two releases:
Core tracking, master data, inbound/outbound order management, return and repair flows, warehouse tooling, and basic analytics.
Demand and supply planning, inventory repositioning, purchase prediction, alerting framework, demand planner role, and API integration with external systems.

The solution will be built as a React web application with a Python FastAPI backend and SQLite database (upgradeable to PostgreSQL), designed for initial local deployment with a clear path to server hosting.

Terminal Distributor is a global distributor of payment terminals operating a network of warehouses and forward stocking locations (FSLs) across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, and South America. Their product portfolio comprises approximately 486 SKUs including payment terminals (serialised), serialised accessories (pin pads, contactless readers), and non-serialised accessories (cables, SIM cards, receipt rolls, batteries).

Terminal Distributor manages high-value, serialised payment devices through a complex lifecycle: from purchase order and inbound receipt, through staging and key injection, to outbound shipment to customers, and back via return and repair. Today, this tracking is fragmented across spreadsheets, ERP exports, and warehouse management systems that do not communicate with each other.

The result is a lack of real-time serial-level visibility, inability to confirm Available-to-Promise dates for sales orders, difficulty managing repair and return flows, and no unified cost tracking per terminal. Additionally, Terminal Distributor manages a global network including suppliers from Europe, USA, and Brazil, serving merchants, shops, distributors, and partners globally.
The application must fulfil the following business objectives:
Monitor the location and status of every terminal by serial number at all times.
Provide real-time counts of terminals by product and by location, across all states.
Track processing costs and first costs per terminal and at aggregate levels.
Identify locations where terminals are missing or in overflow, and support repositioning decisions.
Enable multiple business personas (Supply Planner, Warehouse User, Repair Centre, Supplier) to collaborate on a single order or serial number record.
Allow planning of terminal transfers from one warehouse to another.
Monitor average dwell time per state, average repair time, transit times, and customer return behaviour.
Manage the full return and repair lifecycle at serial number level.
On outbound Sales Orders, confirm the delivery date and fulfilling location instantly based on current inventory.
Forecast the need for new terminal purchases from suppliers based on demand signals.
Manage all reference data — products, BOMs, suppliers, warehouses, customers, terminal states, activity costs, and transit rules.
Product Master & BOM, Supplier Master, Warehouse/Location Master, Customer Master, Terminal State Configuration, Activity Cost Master
Full state machine for serialised products; counts for non-serialised accessories
Purchase Order creation & management; serial number import via Excel upload; warehouse receipt confirmation
Sales, Replacement, Rental, and Distribution order types; full order lifecycle workflow; Box/kit fulfillment with ATP check
Return Order flow; auto-prompt to create linked Replacement Order; repair dispatch and repair cost capture
Bulk receipt confirmation for a PO; bulk shipment confirmation across orders
Inventory dashboard, state distribution, dwell times, order fulfillment metrics
Admin, Supply Planner, Warehouse User, Repair Centre; role-based access control with login
Prepared structure for future GET/POST/PATCH integration with external Logistics API
Demand Planner role; demand signal management; forward demand forecasting
Safety stock targets; replenishment planning; inventory gap/overflow identification
Plan and execute inter-warehouse transfers based on demand vs. supply balance
Forecast new purchase orders from suppliers based on demand signals and lead times
Configurable alert rules (e.g., rental expiry warning, return receipt notification)
Live GET import and POST/PATCH export with TERMINAL DISTRIBUTOR Logistics API
Out of scope for both releases: ERP integration, carrier booking, financial reporting, invoice generation.
The following roles exist in the application. Each role controls what a user can see and what actions they can initiate.
System administrator. Configures master data, manages users and states.
Full access: all master data CRUD, user management, state configuration, cost master, system settings
Creates and manages outbound orders. Monitors inventory and order status.
Create/edit outbound orders (Sales, Replacement, Rental, Distribution); view all inventory; view KPI dashboard
Receives inbound shipments, confirms state changes, performs mass uploads.
Confirm receipt of POs; confirm shipment of orders; mass upload state changes; update serial number states
Manages terminals dispatched for repair. Confirms repair completion and costs.
View repair queue; confirm repair done; enter actual repair costs; update terminal state post-repair
Manages demand signals and forward-looking demand data.
Create/edit demand signals; view planning dashboard; collaborate on supply plan

All master data is managed by the Admin role. Master data forms the configuration backbone of the application and must be in place before operational flows can function. All master data entities support Excel bulk upload for initial population and ongoing maintenance.
The product master and bill-of-materials (BOM) configuration are unified into a single entity. Each product record contains:
Boolean — if Yes, the product is tracked at serial number level; if No, tracked by count only
Enumerated: PaymentDevice | SerializedAccessory | Accessory (aligns with source system categories)
Optional — standard cost for refurbished units
Pipe-separated list of applicable regions (e.g., EU|UK|US|AU)
Optional — list of interchangeable SKU codes for substitution
Optional — customs classification code for cross-border shipments
Boolean — if Yes, the product is a kit/box containing multiple components
If Is BOM = Yes, a list of component product codes with quantities (e.g., 1x terminal + 2x cables + 1x receipt roll)
Many-to-many link to Supplier Master — multiple suppliers can supply the same product
Flag to deactivate products without deletion
Admin can add and remove BOM components from an existing product record via the UI. Excel upload is available for bulk creation and update of product records.

Each supplier record contains: Supplier Code, Supplier Name, Country, City/Location, Contact details (optional), and a list of Products Supplied (linked from Product Master). Suppliers are assigned in the Product Master and visible here as a reference view.
Unique short code (e.g., Oostrum, DHLAU, FSLUK)
Enumerated: Warehouse | FSL | Repair Centre | Supplier
Geographic service area (e.g., Europe, North America)
Configurable matrix of lead times to other locations (days by transport mode: Air / Sea / Road)
Transit time matrix is used by the order allocation engine to calculate ATP dates when stock is not immediately co-located.
Optional — for risk flagging on orders
Terminal states are configurable master data, managed exclusively by the Admin role. States apply only to serialised products. The configuration screen allows Admins to:
Add a new state (code, display name, description, warehouse type classification)
Define which role(s) may trigger a transition to each state
Define valid predecessor states (state transition rules)
The default state set shipped with Release 1 is as follows:
Purchase Order creation / inbound file upload
PO raised; serial assigned but not yet received at warehouse
VAS activities in progress (firmware, kitting, battery charge, packaging)
Shipped to customer on a Sales Order
Delivered to and confirmed by customer
Delivery attempt failed at customer location
Terminal returned as defective; RMA process initiated
At repair centre; repair in progress
Returned from repair; awaiting quality check
Refurbished and available to sell or distribute
The Activity Cost Master defines the standard cost of each warehouse or logistics activity, forming the basis for per-terminal cost tracking. Each record contains:
The location where the activity occurs
The state or activity the cost is associated with (e.g., QUARANTINE, STAGING, TRANSIT_TO_COMPANY)
If cost varies by product or kit, a product-level override can be specified
Currency of the cost (costs may differ per warehouse, e.g., EUR for Oostrum, USD for Memphis, CHF for others)
For IN_REPAIR activities, the standard cost is a placeholder. The Repair Centre user enters the actual repair cost upon completion.
Every serialised terminal (PaymentDevice or SerializedAccessory) is tracked at serial number level. The serial number record contains:
Unique identifier assigned by the manufacturer
Current terminal state (from the configurable state set)
PO ID and PO Line ID
SO ID and SO Line ID (if applicable)
If terminal has been moved or dispatched
Complete chronological log of all state changes, with timestamp, actor (user or API), and optional notes
Running total of activity costs incurred against this serial number
The serial number detail view shows the full genealogy/history of a terminal — every state it has been through, when, by whom, and with what references.
Non-serialised accessories (cables, SIM cards, receipt rolls, batteries, etc.) are tracked by quantity per location. Each record contains:
Received (in warehouse, not yet made available) | Available
Non-serialised inventory can be adjusted manually by Warehouse Users or updated via mass upload. There is no state machine beyond Received and Available.
The application provides the following standard inventory views:
All Terminals — searchable and filterable list of all serial numbers
By State — grouped view of all terminals by their current state
By Location — inventory counts (serialised + non-serialised) per warehouse or FSL
By Product — count of available, in-transit, in-repair units per SKU
Expecting (Inbound) — all terminals with state EXPECTING, linked to open POs
Available-to-Promise — queryable ATP check: for a given product and quantity, which location can fulfil, and by when
Purchase Orders (POs) are the genesis document for new terminal serial numbers. A PO record contains:
List of product lines (product code + expected quantity)
Estimated date of arrival at destination warehouse
Enumerated: Draft | Issued | Partially Received | Fully Received | Closed | Cancelled

Supply Planners create POs in the system. When a PO is created, the expected serial numbers are not yet known — they are populated via the serial number import (see 6.3.2) once the supplier provides them.
When a supplier ships goods, they provide a file containing the serial numbers of the shipped terminals linked to the PO. The warehouse or supply planner uploads this file into the application.
Warehouse User or Supply Planner selects the relevant PO and uploads the serial number Excel file (format based on the established inbound template).
The system parses the file and creates a serial number record for each entry with state = EXPECTING, linked to the PO.
If a serial number already exists in the system, the import highlights the conflict for review.
Once imported, the serial numbers appear in the Expecting view and the PO line shows the expected count.
The inbound file format is based on the sample SerialNumbers_inbound file. Required columns: SerialNumber, ProductCode. Optional columns: ProductState, Location, PurchaseOrderId, TrackingNumber.
When physical goods arrive at the warehouse:
Warehouse User opens the relevant PO from the Expecting view.
The user confirms receipt — either individually per serial number or via mass confirmation of all serials under the PO.
Confirmed serials transition from EXPECTING to QUARANTINE.
The system records the receipt date, the receiving Warehouse User, and the destination location.
The PO status updates to Partially Received or Fully Received accordingly.
Mass confirmation allows the Warehouse User to select all expected serial numbers under a PO and confirm receipt in a single action, specifying the receipt date.
Outbound Orders are created by Supply Planners and represent any movement of terminals away from a warehouse — to customers, to other warehouses, or as rentals or replacements.
Standard sale of terminals to a merchant, shop, distributor, or partner
Replacement of a defective terminal returned by a customer. Linked to a Return Order.
Temporary deployment of terminals to a customer. Rental period and rental fees apply. Terminal expected back at end of rental period.
Transfer of terminals from one warehouse to another. Ship-to is selected from a dropdown of warehouse codes.
All outbound orders follow a structured lifecycle:
Order created but not yet submitted. Editable.
Order submitted and confirmed. Sent to warehouse queue.
Specific serial numbers have been allocated to this order by the system.
Warehouse User has acknowledged the order and is physically picking items.
Warehouse User confirms shipment. Captures: Carrier, Tracking Number, Shipped Date, Estimated Arrival Date, Shipping Cost.
Delivery confirmed (by carrier POD or customer confirmation).
If delivery is unsuccessful, the order status moves to Delivery Failed. The Warehouse User or Supply Planner can initiate a retry or trigger a Return flow.
Orders can be cancelled from Draft or Issued status. Allocated serials are released back to Available.
When creating an outbound order, the Supply Planner specifies:
One or more order lines, each specifying: Product Code (or Box/BOM code) and Quantity

When a BOM/Box product code is selected, the system automatically expands the line into all component SKUs (as defined in the Product Master BOM configuration) and checks availability of all components.
The order allocation engine performs an Available-to-Promise (ATP) check at order creation or on demand:
For each order line (or BOM-expanded component), the system checks current AVAILABLE inventory at the preferred fulfillment location.
If all components of a BOM are co-located at a single location → allocation is instant, ATP date = today + transit time to customer.

If components are split across locations → the system identifies the missing components, checks inventory at other locations, and calculates the lead time required to consolidate stock at the fulfillment location using the Transit Time master data.
The ATP result is presented to the Supply Planner before the order is issued, showing: fulfilling location, expected ship date, expected delivery date.
The Supply Planner can accept the ATP result or adjust the order (change quantity, product, or source location).
Specific serial number allocation happens at the Allocated stage of the workflow, not at order creation. The ATP check confirms count availability only.
Rental orders include two additional fields beyond standard Sales:
Duration of the rental, defaulting to 12 months (configurable per order).

The system tracks the rental end date (Shipped Date + Rental Period) for each rental order. When the rental period ends, the terminal is expected to be returned by the customer. The Return flow handles the physical return of rented terminals.
Rental expiry alerts are planned for Release 2 as part of the Alerting Framework.
Replacement orders are created in response to a Return Order. The intended flow is:
Customer notifies of a defective terminal. A Return Order is created (see 6.5.1).
Upon creating the Return Order, the system automatically prompts the Supply Planner to create a linked Replacement Order for the same product and the same customer.
The Replacement Order is linked to the Return Order by reference. Both are visible from each other's detail view.
The Replacement Order follows the standard outbound order workflow.
A Return Order is created when a terminal is returned by a customer (defective, end of rental, or other reason). The Return Order record contains:
Linked order from which the terminal was shipped
Defective | End of Rental | Wrong Item | Other
Initiated | In Transit | Received | Inspected | Closed

When the Return Order status moves to Received, the terminal serial number state transitions to DEFECT. The system prompts the Supply Planner to initiate a Replacement Order if the reason is Defective.
Once a returned terminal is under investigation or confirmed defective, the Warehouse User or Supply Planner can dispatch it to a Repair Centre:
A Repair Dispatch record is created, linking the serial number(s) and the target Repair Centre location.
Repair Centre User receives the terminal and confirms receipt → state transitions to IN_REPAIR.
Repair Centre User completes the repair and confirms completion, entering: actual repair cost (amount + currency), repair notes (optional), and outcome (Repaired | Beyond Repair).
If Repaired → terminal state transitions to QUARANTINE_REFURBISHED and returns to the originating warehouse. After quality check, Warehouse User moves it to AVAILABLE_REFURBISHED.
If Beyond Repair → terminal state transitions to DESTROYED.
The Mass Upload feature is designed for Warehouse Users to process high-volume operations efficiently without serial-by-serial data entry.
Upload or select all serial numbers under a given PO and confirm receipt in bulk. System updates all selected serials from EXPECTING to QUARANTINE with a single action.

Confirm shipment of multiple orders (potentially a mix of Sales and Distribution order types) in a single upload. The user specifies the shipped date and the system updates all selected order lines and serial numbers accordingly.
Upload a file mapping serial numbers to new states, for bulk state corrections or transitions (Admin or authorised Warehouse User only).
Upload a file to adjust counts of non-serialised accessories per location.
All mass uploads are logged in the audit trail with the uploading user, timestamp, file name, and number of records processed. Errors are reported per row with a downloadable error report.
The KPI dashboard provides operational visibility across the terminal network. Available in Release 1:
Count of terminals in each state, across all locations. Filterable by product, location, and stock type.
Quantity per product per warehouse/FSL. Includes serialised and non-serialised.
Average number of days a terminal spends in each state. Identifies bottlenecks (e.g., long staging time).
Average days from TRANSIT_TO_REPAIR to QUARANTINE_REFURBISHED, per repair centre.
Average days in transit per lane (origin → destination), by transport mode.
Percentage of orders delivered on or before the committed ATP date.
Volume of Return Orders by customer, reason, and product over a rolling period.
Total accumulated activity costs per serial number. Exportable to Excel.
List of rental orders approaching expiry, sorted by expiry date.

The application will be architected to support future integration with the TERMINAL DISTRIBUTOR Logistics API. In Release 1, the API module exists as a structural placeholder with the following design:
Scheduled or on-demand pull of PO, serial number, distribution, and dispatch data from the external Logistics API. Data maps into the local application database.
Push of state changes, order confirmations, and receipt updates from the local application back to the external system.
In Release 1, the module is not activated but its schema, endpoint configuration, and data mapping layer are prepared as stubs. In Release 2, the module is enabled and configurable by Admin.
Application must load any inventory list view within 3 seconds for up to 10,000 serial number records. Search and filter results must return within 2 seconds.

Release 1 is designed for hundreds of active serial numbers and dozens of concurrent orders. Database schema and architecture must allow migration to PostgreSQL for larger scale without application code changes.
Release 1: local desktop deployment. Release 2: target 99.5% uptime on server deployment.
All state transitions are logged with timestamp, user, and source (UI or API). No state change is possible without a valid preceding state per the state transition rules defined in master data.
Complete, immutable history of every serial number state change and every order status change must be stored and viewable.
All users must authenticate via username and password. Passwords are hashed. Role-based access control enforced at API level. JWT-based session tokens.
The application supports Excel upload for all master data entities and for the inbound serial number file. All list views are exportable to Excel.
Modern browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox (latest 2 versions).
Release 1: runs locally via a single start command. Release 2: deployable to a Linux server with standard setup instructions.
UI in English. Currency fields support multi-currency. No locale-specific formatting requirements in R1.
Fast development, component-based UI, hot reload for iteration speed. Vite provides lean local dev server.
Utility-first CSS with e2open colour palette configured as custom tokens. Clean, responsive layout without heavy dependencies.
Icons for each module (Inventory, Orders, Master Data, Analytics, Admin). e2open colour scheme (navy #003087, blue #0075C2).
Modern, high-performance Python API framework. Auto-generates OpenAPI docs. Easy to extend for API integration module.
Database-agnostic ORM. Allows seamless migration from SQLite (local) to PostgreSQL (server) by changing connection string only.
SQLite requires zero infrastructure for local use. PostgreSQL migration is a one-step upgrade for server deployment.
Stateless auth with role claims embedded in the token. Refresh token for session persistence.
Excel file parsing for inbound serial number files and master data uploads.
Placeholder endpoints for future Logistics API GET/POST operations.
The backend is structured as independent FastAPI routers, one per domain. Each module has its own data models, API endpoints, and service layer:
auth — user authentication, JWT token management, role enforcement
products — product master, BOM management, supplier-product relationships
locations — warehouse and FSL master CRUD, transit time matrix
states — configurable terminal state definitions and transition rules
activity_costs — cost master per state per location
inventory — serial number records, state transitions, non-serialised counts
purchase_orders — PO management, expected serial tracking
inbound — serial number file upload and import processing
outbound_orders — Sales, Replacement, Rental, and Distribution order management
returns — Return Order management and repair dispatch
mass_upload — bulk state update and shipment confirmation endpoints
analytics — aggregated KPI queries and dashboard data
api_integration — stub module for future Logistics API connectivity
Core database entities and their relationships:
Product — linked to BOMComponent, Supplier (many-to-many via ProductSupplier)
SerialNumber — linked to Product, Location, OutboundOrder, PurchaseOrder, StateHistory
StateHistory — immutable log record per serial number state change
PurchaseOrder — linked to Supplier, Location, PurchaseOrderLine → SerialNumber
OutboundOrder — linked to Customer or Location (for distribution), OutboundOrderLine → SerialNumber
ReturnOrder — linked to OutboundOrder, SerialNumber, optional link to Replacement OutboundOrder
RepairDispatch — linked to SerialNumber, Repair Centre location, actual cost
NonSerialisedInventory — linked to Product, Location, state, quantity
ActivityCostMaster — linked to Location, state/activity, optional Product
User — linked to Role; role controls permissions across all modules
Release 1 delivers the full core tracking, master data, and order management capability of the application. It is the foundation on which Release 2 planning features are built.

R1 API Stub, all R1 data models
In R1, carrier tracking numbers are manually entered. No live carrier API integration. Delivery confirmation is manual or via mass upload.
No ERP integration in scope. The application is a standalone master of record for terminal tracking. Financial data (invoices, credit notes) remains in ERP.
Alerting for rental expiry (1 week before end date) is deferred to Release 2 Alerting Framework.
Transit time matrix will be pre-loaded with known lanes. Unknown lanes will default to a configurable fallback (e.g., 14 days). Admin can complete the matrix post-deployment.
The Supplier role was considered but deferred. Suppliers do not have a login in R1. Inbound file upload is handled by Warehouse User or Supply Planner.
These states from the source system are excluded from the configurable state set for R1. They can be added by Admin via the State Configuration if needed.
NON_P2PE_DEPLOYED and NON_P2PE_NOT_IN_USE are excluded from the default state set. Admin can add them if required.
Customer credit rating is stored as a master data field but credit limit enforcement (block orders above limit) is not in R1 scope.
